7.25 On being asked, the purpose of having separate hostel for OBC students the Department 
of Social Justice and Empowerment submitted vide written reply that: 
 
“The provision of separate hostels for OBC students is primarily intended as a 
supportive measure to improve access to education for students from socially and 
educationally disadvantaged backgrounds, particularly those coming from remote or 
economically weaker families. If seats reserved for OBC remains vacant, it would be 
filled up in following preference:-  
 
(a) De-notified Tribes (DNT) students 
(b) Scheduled Tribes (ST) Students 
(c) Scheduled Caste (SC) Students 
(d) Economically Weaker Section (EWS) Students 
 
The objective is not segregation, but facilitation of safe, affordable accommodation 
where such facilities are otherwise inadequate. Care is taken to ensure that these 
hostels function as part of the larger campus ecosystem, with students participating 
fully in academic, cultural and extracurricular activities alongside their peers. 
Institutions are advised to promote inclusivity and equal opportunity so that no sense 

73  
of isolation or stigma arises. The overall approach is developmental and welfare-
oriented, aimed at strengthening educational participation without compromising 
social integration.” 
 
7.26 On being enquired with regard to assessment was conducted prior to launch of the 
Scheme, the Department of Social Justice and Empowerment stated in their written reply that: 
 
“Department of Social Justice and Empowerment undertook preliminary assessments 
of the need for hostel facilities based on the number of eligible students, gaps in 
existing infrastructure, and regional educational backwardness. These assessments 
drew on data from State Governments, enrolment statistics, and demand projections 
for residential facilities for OBC students. While the scheme originally aimed at 
constructing hostels in phases, the timeline for completion varied by project 
depending on availability of land, administrative approvals, tendering processes, and 
release of funds by both Central and State Governments.” 
 
 
 
7.27 On being asked about the norms laid down for constructions of hostels sanctioned along 
with the number of Hostels constructed within the stipulated period including reasons for delay 
and the action taken thereon, the Department of Social Justice and Empowerment stated in their 
written reply that: 
 
“Cost norms are prescribed per seat by region and funding is shared between Centre 
and States/UTs (60:40 for boys, 90:10 for girls; 100% for UTs; 90:10 for Central 
institutions), with a mandatory completion period of 18 months from award of work 
order or 2 years from release of central assistance whichever is earlier, and any cost 
escalation due to delay is to be borne by the State/Institute. It has been noted that 
significant delays have occurred in completing sanctioned hostels, with few 
completed within the stipulated timelines and many remaining incomplete due to 
funding flow issues, administrative/approval bottlenecks, land acquisition and 
procurement delays, tendering and contracting slowdowns, and late release of 
matching State share. Detailed State/Institution‑wise sanctioned vs constructed 
numbers and exact reasons for delay are not maintained by the Ministry; however, 
parliamentary responses and audit observations have highlighted delays in several 
State implementations and noted efforts to review progress and improve monitoring. 
States and implementing agencies have been encouraged through official 
communications to expedite execution, ensure timely release of matching share, 
adhere strictly to prescribed timelines, and improve project management to minimise 
further delays and ensure students benefit from the hostel infrastructure.”

7.38 The Committee note that the Department of Social Justice and Empowerment has 
neither been able to exhaust the budgetary allocation nor achieve the targets fixed for 
2023-24, 2024-25 and 2025-26 under various components of PM-YASASVI. The Committee 
find that certain procedural issues such as pending Aadhaar seeding, bank account 
validation, utilization certificates (UCs), etc., are challenges before the Department in 
optimizing the utilization of resources and maximizing the targets laid down under the 
Scheme. The Committee note that despite various measures such as periodic review, 
third party evaluation, awareness of Scheme, etc. taken by the Department to address the 
challenges in implementing the schemes these challenges continue to recur year after 
year. The Committee have no doubt about the sincerity of the Department, but it would 
appreciate if suitable steps are taken so that the issues hampering the Scheme dies down 
once and for all and the Scheme is  smoothly implemented. 
The Committee also note that the income eligibility has been enhanced from ₹2.5 
lakh to ₹4.5 lakh by the Department and has also introduced disability allowance of 
₹10,000 per annum from 2026-27. However, the Committee find that the Budgetary 
Estimate for 2025-26 has not increased for most of the sub-components of the Scheme 
for the year 2026-27. The Committee expect that the expenditure on the sub-components 
may multiply as the number of applicants may increase with the enhanced income 
eligibility and disability allowance.  The Committee would therefore, like the Department 
to timely assess the funds requirement for the year 2026-27 to meet the increased demand 
under each sub-component of the Scheme. The Committee believe that the Department 
will take all necessary measures to ensure that no applicant is deprived of the Scheme 
for want of funds. The Committee would like to be informed in this regard. 
7.39 The Committee note that the target fixed for 2024-25 under Post Matric Scholarship 
Scheme was not achieved and the same target was again fixed for 2025-26. The 
Committee are not sure about the status of achievement vis-a-vis the target fixed for 2025-
26 as the Committee have been informed that the details of Beneficiaries are not available 
with them and will be available only when the proposal for 2026-27 are received from the 
State/UT Government. The Committee are surprised to find that the target for 2026-27 has 
been reduced to 34 lakhs in comparison to previous two years. The Committee feel that 
the approach of the Department appears to be that if you are not able to achieve the goal 

78  
it is better to bring down the goal so that you don’t have to face the failure. The Committee 
are not satisfied with the way the Scheme is being implemented by the Department as 
they strongly feel that the Scheme can be considered successful only if the target fixed 
are achieved and the target for next year are enhanced.  The Committee are of the opinion 
that the target fixed should increase every year so that the revised estimates also 
increase consequently. 
 The Committee are happy to note that a proposal has been submitted for revision 
of the scheme to the Expenditure Finance Committee with regard to the income ceiling 
and scholarship rates. In view of the proposed revision, the Committee feel that the 
budgetary allocation made may not be sufficient as the number of beneficiaries is likely 
to increase significantly. The Committee hope that the Department will make all efforts to 
implement the proposals from 2026-27 and seek enhancement of the budget at the RE 
stage to meet the requirement of funds so that students do not suffer. The Committee 
expect that the proposal will be approved urgently so that the beneficiaries get the benefit 
in the year 2026-27 itself.  The Committee would like to be apprised of the effect of the

ATAL VAYO ABHYUDAY YOJANA (AVYAY) 
The Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment (MoSJE) is the nodal Ministry for the 
welfare of senior citizens. In alignment with the principles of active and healthy ageing and to 
ensure dignified living for the elderly, the Ministry is implementing the umbrella scheme Atal 
Vayo Abhyudaya Yojana (AVYAY). AVYAY seeks to provide comprehensive and integrated 
services through the convergence of various interventions targeted at different aspects of elderly 
welfare ranging from shelter and medical care to assistive devices, helpline services and 
caregiver training. The components under AVYAY are as follows: - 
 
INTEGRATED PROGRAMME FOR SENIOR CITIZENS (IPSRC) 
 
8.2 The objective of the IPSrC is to enhance the quality of life of senior citizens, particularly 
indigent elderly persons, by providing essential amenities such as shelter, food, medical care 
and recreational facilities, while promoting productive and active ageing. Under the scheme, 
financial assistance in the form of grant-in-aid is provided to eligible implementing agencies, 
including NGOs and voluntary organizations, for the operation and maintenance of various 
facilities, including Senior Citizens’ Homes for 25 beneficiaries, Senior Citizens’ Homes for 50 
beneficiaries (male only or combined male and female), Senior Citizens’ Homes exclusively for 
50 elderly women, Continuous Care Homes and homes for senior citizens suffering from 
Alzheimer’s disease or dementia for a minimum of 20 beneficiaries, Regional Resource and 
Training Centers, and Mobile Medicare Units (MMUs) and Physiotherapy Clinics for senior 
citizens. 
 
STATE ACTION PLAN FOR SENIOR CITIZENS (SAPSRC) 
 
8.3 The State Action Plan for Senior Citizens (SAPSrC) is a component of the Atal Vayo 
Abhudaya Yojana (AVYAY) under which financial assistance is provided to States and Union 
Territories to implement state-specific initiatives for the welfare of senior citizens, with a primary 
focus on cataract surgeries for senior citizens, training of geriatric caregivers, awareness 
generation about the scheme, and any other activities considered appropriate by the States/UTs 
to improve the well-being of senior citizens. 
 
RASHTRIYA VAYOSHRI YOJANA (RVY) 
 
8.4 Rashtriya Vayoshri Yojana (RVY) was first announced in the 2015-16 Union Budget 
speech by the finance minister and subsequently launched on 01st April, 2017. The objective of 
the scheme is to provide eligible senior citizens suffering from any of the age-related disability/ 
infirmity, with assisted living devices which can restore near normalcy in their bodily functions, 

81  
overcoming the disability/ infirmity manifested such as low vision, hearing impairment, loss of 
teeth and loco-motor disabilities. 
  
ELDERLINE: NATIONAL HELPLINE FOR SENIOR CITIZENS (NHSC) 
 
8.5 National Helpline for Senior Citizens was dedicated to the Nation on 01st October, 2021 
on the occasion of the International Day of Older Persons, with the toll-free number 14567. 
Elderline operates for 12 hours a day (8:00 AM to 8:00 PM) and provides free information, 
guidance, emotional support and field intervention in cases of abuse, neglect and rescue. The 
National Institute of Social Defence, an autonomous body under MoSJE, is the nodal agency for 
implementation of Elderline across the country. 
 
 
SENIOR CARE AGEING GROWTH ENGINE (SAGE) 
 
8.6 SAGE portal was dedicated to the Nation on 01 October 2021. The scheme aims to 
encourage entrepreneurs and start-ups to develop innovative solutions to address challenges 
faced by the elderly. Under the scheme, Government of India support is provided to start-ups 
through equity participation of up to 49%, with assistance up to ₹1 crore, to promote elder-care 
innovations. 
 
SYSTEM FOR PROVISION OF ELDERCARE IN-HOUSE AND ASSISTED LIVING (PM 
SPECIAL)/ TRAINING OF GERIATRIC CARE GIVERS 
 
8.7 The main objective of the PM Special (Training of Geriatric Care Givers) scheme is to 
bridge the gap in supply and increasing demand in the field of geriatric caregivers so as to 
provide more professional services to the senior citizens and also to create a cadre of 
professional caregivers in the field of geriatrics. The Scheme will ensure sufficient availability of 
dedicated, professionally trained manpower of geriatric caregivers who can attend to diverse 
and dynamic needs of elderly population relating to recreation and holistic well-being. So far, 
35,480 trainees have been imparted training under the scheme.

NATIONAL ACTION FOR MECHANIZED SANITATION ECOSYSTEM (NAMASTE) 
 
NAMASTE, a joint initiative of the MoSJE and the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs 
(MoHUA), is being implemented since FY 2023-24. The scheme envisages safety and dignity of 
sanitation workers by creating an enabling ecosystem that recognizes sanitation workers as one 
of the key contributors in operations and maintenance of sanitation infrastructure thereby 
enhancing their occupational safety through capacity building and improved access to safety 
gear and machines. Components of erstwhile Self Employment Scheme for Rehabilitation of 
Manual Scavengers (SRMS) have been subsumed in NAMASTE scheme from 2023-24. Further, 
waste pickers have been added as target group under NAMASTE in FY 2024-25. The Key 
Interventions of the scheme are as follows:- 
 
A. Sewer and Septic tank Workers (SSWs) 
Interventions  
(i) Profiling of Sewer/ Septic Tank workers. 
(ii) Distribution of Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) kits to identified 
SSWs 
(iii) Distribution of safety devices to ERSUs 
(iv) Imparting occupational safety training to SSWs 
(v) Health insurance coverage of SSWs and manual scavengers and their 
dependents under Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY (after profiling of SSWs by 
ULBs) 
(vi) Upfront capital subsidy upto ₹7.50 Lakh for individual projects costing upto 
₹ 15.00 lakh for sanitation related projects and capital subsidy of ₹25.00 
Lakh for a group project of five sanitation workers including manual 
scavengers for a project costing ₹ 50.00 Lakh. 
(vii)Appointment of Responsible Sanitation Authority (RSA) in every District. 
(viii)Constitution of Emergency Response Sanitation Unit (ERSU) in larger 
Urban Local Bodies (ULB) of Districts to cover Urban and Rural areas.  
(ix) Operationalization of Helpline number (14420). 
(x) IEC Campaign: Targeting Safai Mitras, Operators/ Contractors and 
Citizensthrough RWAs etc. through print and digital media, innovative 
media interventions and by organizing workshops/webinars 
  

91  
B.  Waste pickers  
Waste Pickers have been included as an additional target group along with sewer 
septic tank workers under NAMASTE scheme. The identified waste pickers would 
later on be provided occupational/ up gradation training for waste value addition. The 
scheme has various components for welfare of waste pickers namely profiling, Health 
Insurance under AB-PMJAY, Social Security Benefits, Occupational Safety Training, 
PPE Kits, Capital Subsidy for Dry Waste Collection Centres (DWCCs) to procure 
Waste Collection Vehicles and other welfare measures. The waste pickers 
component of the Scheme intends to integrate waste pickers in the solid waste 
management by addressing challenges, difficulties faced by them by mainstreaming 
them in the society, recognizing and strengthening their contribution in waste 
collection, recovery & recycling, providing safe, dignified and sustainable livelihood 
by empowering them through various interventions. Department of Social Justice & 
Empowerment, Ministry of Health & Family Welfare, National Health Authority, 
National Safai Karamcharis Finance and Development Corporation, Ayushman 
Bharat Empanelled Hospitals and Waste Pickers are the major stakeholders. The 
core objective of the Scheme is to ensure that waste pickers live dignified lives and 
work in a safe environment by enabling their enumeration, recognition and integration 
into the solid waste management value chain, while ensuring access to social security 
and welfare schemes based on their occupational identity.

9.13 The Committee note that the Department of Social Justice s Empowerment, in a 
joint initiative with the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs, has been implementing the 
‘NAMASTE’ scheme since 2023-24 for the safety and dignity of sanitation workers 
comprising Manual Scavengers, Sewer and Septic Tank Workers. The Department has 
also included waste pickers under the scheme since 2024-25. The Committee are happy 
to note that the Department of Social Justice and Empowerment has also proposed a new 
target group consisting of drain-cleaners, workers at Sewage Treatment Plants and 
Faecal Sludge Treatment Plants during the next financial cycle, i.e., 2026-27 to 2030-31. 
The Committee finds that 89,248 Sewer and Septic Tank Workers and 1,87,120 waste 
pickers have been validated, out of which 87,037 Sewer and Septic Tank Workers and 
7,499 waste pickers have been provided PPE kits. The Committee appreciate the 
measures such as occupational safety training, safety devices, workshops, health 
insurance coverage, etc., taken by the Department since the initiation of the scheme in 
2023-24. However, the Committee are of the opinion that profiling, distribution of PPE kits 
and provision of occupational safety training to all sanitation workers will require greater 
effort, time and funds. The Department of Social Justice and Empowerment should 
therefore expedite the process and lay down a time frame to complete all necessary steps 
for the economic and social welfare of sanitation workers.  
  The Committee also feel that the funds provided under the scheme need to be 
increased, as the Department has already spent 93% of the Revised Estimate for 2025-26, 
therefore, the allocation of ₹110.00 crore made for 2026-27 may not be sufficient to 
complete the tasks undertaken by the Department as a large number of workers are still 
to be provided PPE kits and other benefits. Further, after the inclusion of the new target 
group from 2026-27 under the scheme, the Department may face a shortage of funds. The 
Committee would therefore like the Department to take sufficient steps so that basic 
facilities such as PPE kits, training and health insurance are provided to all workers at 
the earliest, and budget constraints should not become a hurdle, especially when several 
deaths of sewer and septic tank workers are still being reported.

Protection of Civil Rights Acts, 1955 (PCR Act, 1955) and Scheduled Castes and Scheduled

(iv) Incentive for Inter-Caste Marriages, where one of the spouse is a member of a 
Scheduled Castes. 
(v)  Awareness generation and publicity.

10.9 The Committee note that the Department of Social Justice and Empowerment is 
the custodian of civic rights and is responsible for the prevention of atrocities against 
Scheduled Castes. Funds are allocated to the Department for strengthening of machinery 
for enforcement of protection of Civil Rights Act,1955 and Prevention of Atrocities Act 
,1989. The Department has accordingly taken measures over the years for the functioning 
and strengthening of Protection Cells and Special Police Stations as envisaged under 
these Acts. The Committee however find that though almost all States/UTs have set up 
Protection Cells but only 181 Special Police Stations have been established in only 7 
States/UTs. The Committee are shocked to know that even after more than three decades 
of enactment of PoA Act only 7 States/UTs have such police stations. The Committee are 
of the opinion that the setting up of Special Police Stations by the States/UTs is essential 
as victims first approach police station for protection at the time of atrocity and it is 
assumed these police stations would be able to address such situations more effectively.  
The Committee do not find any information regarding setting up of Special Courts also. 
The regular meetings with the State government over the years have also failed to yield 
the desired result. 
The Committee note that the Department has submitted a proposal before the 
Expenditure Finance Committee (EFC) to enhance the relief amounts and provide 
financial support to States for setting up Special Police Stations and Special Courts. The 
Committee hope that the Department should have incorporated the expected increase in 
funds for the year 2026-27 so that there is no shortage of funds to meet the expenditure 
likely to increase with the approval of the proposal. The Committee accordingly desire 
that the Department should take necessary steps to ensure that the proposal is approved 
at the earliest so that it is implemented from 2026-27 itself and the machinery is 
adequately strengthened.

students are not deprived of the Scheme as they have a 
dedicated budget for the targeted caste. 
11. 8.23 The Committee are happy to note that the Department of 
Social Justice and Empowerment has been allocated 
₹740.00 crore for the year 2026-27 under Atal Vayo 
Abhyuday Yojana (AVYAY), over and above the allocations 
made for 2023-24, 2024-25 and 2025-26. Unfortunately, the 
Department was not able to spend the Revised Estimate for 
2024-25 and has been able to spend only 60% of the 
allocation in 2025-26. The Committee hope that the 
Department will be able to spend the Budgetary Allocation 
for 2025-26 and would take necessary initiatives to rule out 
the reasons such as delays in approval, revision of scheme 
guidelines, etc., resulting in under-utilisation of funds. The 
Committee expect that the changes proposed to the 
Expenditure Finance Committee (EFC) will be approved at 
the earliest  so that the senior citizens can reap the benefits 
of the changes proposed from 2026-27 onwards and the 
budget allocated for 2026-27 is  also fully utilised.  
 
 8.24 The Committee have been made to understand that the 
Department proposes to associate State/UT governments 
for the smooth implementation of Schemes and also 
proposes to increase funding limit to Start ups under 
SAGE, increase in daily food nutrition, etc.  As per the 
proposal the Centre and State would be sharing 

127  
expenditure in the ratio of 60:40. The Committee are sure 
that the measures being proposed would enhance the 
performance of the Scheme in the interest of senior citizens 
but they are apprehensive for the 40% share of State 
government. The Committee do not want the Scheme to 
suffer for want of funds from State Governments. 
Therefore, they would like Department to take 
precautionary steps so that States timely contribute their 
share and the Schemes are implemented flawlessly.  The 
Committee would also like the Department to ensure that 
the proposal under submission is approved at the earliest 
so that the proposal is implemented from 2026-27 onwards. 
 
 
 
8.25 The Committee appreciate the efforts of the Department 
and the initiatives taken by it for the welfare of Senior 
Citizens over the years. In order to have better management 
the Department has proposed to associate State/UT 
Governments in the implementation of the Schemes.  The 
Committee also feel that the available machinery with the 
senior citizens Division of the Department is not sufficient 
to cater to the requirement of the senior citizens. The 
Department has also received suggestions from various 
quarters for a separate dedicated Department for the 
welfare of senior citizens. The Department should examine 
the infrastructure available in the Department to manage 
the affairs of Senior Citizens. As is already known that the 
population of Senior Citizens in the country is projected to 
increase from 8.4% to 14.9% of the total population by 2036, 
and a small Division in the Department cannot be expected 
to cater to the increasing population of senior citizens. The 
Committee would also like to draw the attention towards 
the creation of separate Department for Divyangjan in 2012 
by the Government. The separate Department was created 
to manage the affairs of comparatively less population of 

128  
Divyangjan in the country and is effectively catering to their 
needs. The Committee would also like to express that once 
the ‘Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior 
Citizens (Amendment) Bill, 2019 is enacted the 
responsibilities of the Division will multiply. In view of the 
large population of Senior Citizens which continues to 
increase every year, the Committee would like the 
Government to examine creation of a separate dedicated 
Department under the Ministry of Social Justice and 
Empowerment as has been created for Divyangjan to 
ensure greater focus on policy matters relating to Senior 
Citizens and better coordination among stakeholders. 
 
 9.13 The Committee note that the Department of Social Justice 
s Empowerment, in a joint initiative with the Ministry of 
Housing and Urban Affairs, has been implementing the 
‘NAMASTE’ scheme since 2023-24 for the safety and 
dignity of sanitation workers comprising Manual 
Scavengers, Sewer and Septic Tank Workers. The 
Department has also included waste pickers under the 
scheme since 2024-25. The Committee are happy to note 
that the Department of Social Justice and Empowerment 
has also proposed a new target group consisting of drain-
cleaners, workers at Sewage Treatment Plants and Faecal 
Sludge Treatment Plants during the next financial cycle, 
i.e., 2026-27 to 2030-31. The Committee finds that 89,248 
Sewer and Septic Tank Workers and 1,87,120 waste pickers 
have been validated, out of which 87,037 Sewer and Septic 
Tank Workers and 7,499 waste pickers have been provided 
PPE kits. The Committee appreciate the measures such as 
occupational safety training, safety devices, workshops, 
health insurance coverage, etc., taken by the Department 
since the initiation of the scheme in 2023-24. However, the 
Committee are of the opinion that profiling, distribution of 

129  
PPE kits and provision of occupational safety training to all 
sanitation workers will require greater effort, time and 
funds. The Department of Social Justice and Empowerment 
should therefore expedite the process and lay down a time 
frame to complete all necessary steps for the economic and 
social welfare of sanitation workers.  
The Committee also feel that the funds provided under the 
scheme need to be increased, as the Department has 
already spent 93% of the Revised Estimate for 2025-26, 
therefore, the allocation of ₹110.00 crore made for 2026-27 
may not be sufficient to complete the tasks undertaken by 
the Department as a large number of workers are still to be 
provided PPE kits and other benefits. Further, after the 
inclusion of the new target group from 2026-27 under the 
scheme, the Department may face a shortage of funds. The 
Committee would therefore like the Department to take 
sufficient steps so that basic facilities such as PPE kits, 
training and health insurance are provided to all workers at 
the earliest, and budget constraints should not become a 
hurdle, especially when several deaths of sewer and septic 
tank workers are still being reported. 
 
 
 10.9 The Committee note that the Department of Social Justice 
and Empowerment is the custodian of civic rights and is 
responsible for the prevention of atrocities against 
Scheduled Castes. Funds are allocated to the Department 
for strengthening of machinery for enforcement of 
protection of Civil Rights Act,1955 and Prevention of 
Atrocities Act ,1989. The Department has accordingly taken 
measures over the years for the functioning and 
strengthening of Protection Cells and Special Police 
Stations as envisaged under these Acts. The Committee 

130  
however find that though almost all States/UTs have set up 
Protection Cells but only 181 Special Police Stations have 
been established in only 7 States/UTs. The Committee are 
shocked to know that even after more than three decades 
of enactment of PoA Act only 7 States/UTs have such 
police stations. The Committee are of the opinion that the 
setting up of Special Police Stations by the States/UTs is 
essential as victims first approach police station for 
protection at the time of atrocity and it is assumed these 
police stations would be able to address such situations 
more effectively.  The Committee do not find any 
information regarding setting up of Special Courts also. 
The regular meetings with the State government over the 
years have also failed to yield the desired result. 
The Committee note that the Department has 
submitted a proposal before the Expenditure Finance 
Committee (EFC) to enhance the relief amounts and 
provide financial support to States for setting up Special 
Police Stations and Special Courts. The Committee hope 
that the Department should have incorporated the 
expected increase in funds for the year 2026-27 so that 
there is no shortage of funds to meet the expenditure likely 
to increase with the approval of the proposal. The 
Committee accordingly desire that the Department should 
take necessary steps to ensure that the proposal is 
approved at the earliest so that it is implemented from 
2026-27 itself and the machinery is adequately 
strengthened.
